title: alert-churn-root-cause-catalog
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, practical catalog to help oncall and owners quickly map ‘alert churn’ symptoms to likely root causes, short-term mitigations, and durable fixes. The goal is to reduce noisy interruption windows from minutes->hours and ensure owners can pick the correct remediation path without hunting through multiple decks or postmortems.

Context and scope:
- Focus: observability/alerting churn that causes frequent pages (flapping, duplicates, high cardinality noise) or sudden SLO-burn alerts related to missing/incorrect telemetry.
- Not in scope: planned release failures, application bugs that always fail tests (those get normal incident process). This is for signal-to-noise and telemetry supplychain issues.

Definitions (quick):
- Alert churn: >10 distinct pages about the same symptom within a 30m window or >50% of alerts resolve and re-fire within 15m.
- Missing metric: exporter/agent stopped exporting a numeric timeseries the rule depends on for >5m.
- SLO-burn alert: alert triggered when SLO burn-rate or error budget projection exceeds threshold.

Quick triage checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Observe: collect the alert signature (rule_id, fired_at, resolved_at, raw_query, labels, endpoint).
2) Scope: are all regions/zones affected? Check per-region dashboards.
3) Telemetry supply: check exporter hosts for restarts (k8s events), agent CPU, eBPF collector logs.
4) Cardinality: inspect distinct label counts for the metric in the last hour. Did cardinality spike?
5) Rollouts: look for any 30m-old deploys (git tag/helm release) that align.
6) Notification pipeline: verify PagerDuty/Slack delivery (is the same alert firing many times because of delivery duplication?).

Root-cause catalog (symptom -> likely cause -> short mitigation -> durable fix):
A) Symptom: identical alert flashes every ~2m for 30+ minutes (flapping)
- Likely causes: flaky exporter restarting; alert rule without sufficient cooldown; histogram/prometheus reset when collector restarts; flaky network to metrics aggregator causing reconnect storms.
- Short mitigation: temporarily increase alert for: 'for: 10m' or add a dedupe window in notification layer; silence by owner if impact low.
- Durable fix: fix exporter stability or add stable heartbeat metric; change rule to use rate() over a longer window or detect restarts via exporter_up metric. Add liveness probes in exporter.

B) Symptom: sudden spike in unique label cardinality causing many per-customer alerts
- Likely causes: instrumentation bug appending unique request IDs into label; tagging library change; rollout added new dimension at high cardinality.
- Short mitigation: add label whitelist in alert rule or aggregate with by() to limit cardinality; mute noisy customer label group.
- Durable fix: revert tagging change; add cardinality limits to SDK; add CI check blocking new label additions above threshold.

C) Symptom: Missing metric for service-x -> SLO burn alert triggers
- Likely causes: exporter crash, aggregator ingestion pipeline error (Kafka backlog), schema migration renamed metric, retention TTL/compaction removed recent points.
- Short mitigation: set SLO alert to use fallback metric or synthetic heartbeat; escalate to infra team if Kafka consumer lag > 5m; page exporter owner.
- Durable fix: add blackbox exporter synthetic heartbeat and route SLO evaluation to use synthetic where appropriate; add metric rename mapping in ingestion layer.

D) Symptom: Single rule produces many duplicate notifications across channels
- Likely causes: dedupe layer misconfigured after recent notification-service deploy; multiple alertmanager replicas not sharing state; webhook retries not honored.
- Short mitigation: disable duplicate webhook retries; mute duplicates in channels; flip traffic to stable notification cluster.
- Durable fix: migrate to sticky dedupe key (cluster + rule_id + fingerprint), add end-to-end tests for notification dedupe.

E) Symptom: Alerts fire on low-volume synthetic tests after midnight only
- Likely causes: retention compaction aligning with midnight windows; TZ misalignment in rule window; maintenance job that rotates credentials causing transient gaps.
- Short mitigation: shift evaluate window or add temporary silence window for synthetic job.
- Durable fix: fix compaction config or ensure synthetic job has separate retention.

Operator playbook stubs (copyable into PD guide):
- If 'missing metric' and exporter_up==0: page exporter owner -> escalate to infra if node REBOOT events present. Post message: "exporter down on {host}; collector PID died at {time}; attempting restart".
- If 'cardinality spike' and new tag deploy within 30m: roll back or deploy partial config to drop tag, then run CI for label usage.
- If 'SLO burn' but internal metrics inexplicably zero: check ingestion consumer lag, then check metric provenance (was it renamed?).

Useful diagnostic queries (promql-ish plain text):
- alerts_fired_total{rule_id=~".*"} by (rule_id) over 1h -> shows hot rules
- count_values("label_count", metric_name{job=~".*"}) by (job) -> approximate label cardinality
- exporter_up{job="service-x-exporter"} -> 0 indicates exporter crash
- consumer_lag_seconds{topic="metrics"} -> if >300 then ingestion delay

Experiment proposals (short):
1) Rolling dedupe window in notification layer: implement application-side 5m suppression keyed by fingerprint and test for 3 weeks on canary team. Measure pages/day. Linked PR: OBS-837.
2) Metric schema registry: require every new label to be registered and validated for cardinality in CI. Pilot on two teams for Q1.
3) Synthetic SLO fallback: dual-evaluate SLO using both production and synthetic heartbeats where appropriate, so that pure telemetry outages don't immediately burn SLO for external-facing customers.

Dashboards to check (suggested panels):
- Alerts per minute (grouped by rule owner) with 1h/24h trend
- Distinct label cardinality per metric (top 20)
- Exporter restarts per host (last 24h)
- Notification delivery duplicates (webhook 5xx + retries)

Owner and action items (short list):
- Aisha: prototype dedupe suppression in notification layer and run 2-week canary (due 2026-03-10) -> linked OBS-837.
- Ben: add exporter liveness metrics and alert for exporter restart frequency (due 2026-02-28).
- Maya: add CI label-cardinality check in sdk-telemetry (PR draft in github repo).
- Ravi: write runbook for 'missing metric' with escalations and Slack templates (due 2026-03-05).

Slack templates (copy into incident channel):
- Title: [SRE] {short_summary} 
- Body: Summary: {one-liner}
  First observed: {time}
  Affected regions: {regions}
  Immediate action: {what we did}
  Owner: {owner}

Open questions / discussion items:
- Do we want automated temporary silences when a rule flaps >5 times in 15 minutes? (pros: reduces noise; cons: could mask real regression).
- Should SLO evaluation be considered a "critical service" with a separate ingestion path / retention?
- How to give product teams visibility when we mute noisy rules so they can avoid getting surprised?

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Consider attaching a per-rule confidence score (0-1) based on historical false positive rate; use it to weight notification urgency.
- Add a 24h noise leaderboard for owners so teams can proactively prune rules.

References and quick links:
- Internal: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OBS/alerting-guidelines
- Jira: SRE-4121 (investigate high-cardinality incidents), OBS-837 (dedupe suppression patch)
